sent_to_model:
ok my nephew show me this thread on the Mile End board, people think we are closing!! and one say the carnets is a scam. I am a bit angry but also it is the opposite, we BOUGHT the building, I wanted to keep the surprise for the reopening but now I have to tell everybody. Can you help me write the answer to the last one (Bergeron)? In English because the board is english. I want people to be happy with me, not a fight, but I have to say clearly about the carnets. Please give the reopening date and time and invite everyone for January 23, thank the supporters and reassure the upstairs tenants too.

- Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré, 5 rue Fairmount corner, open since March 2009
- building owner M. Ferland 81 yrs old, retiring to Sherbrooke with his daughter, he offer to sell to me before anybody, signed at the notary 15 december
- closed 4 to 18 january for works, reopen Tuesday January 19 at 7h
- new deck oven 4 decks coming from Laval supplier, the old one is from 1998 and break 3 times this year
- we take the space at the back (old storage of the dépanneur) — 6 small tables, finally people can sit
- carnets — sold 214 in october, $60 for 12 loaves, all still good, no expiry + 1 free croissant for each carnet holder in january
- the 3 apartments upstairs stay rented, same tenants same rent, I promise them in writing
- the sign was written by my nephew Thomas at 6h in the morning, "grande nouvelle" was his idea, I said ok without thinking
- the half empty shelves on the 28 is because we sold everything for Christmas eve, 400 bûches, nothing to do with closing
- M. Ferland come every morning for 17 years for his baguette pas trop cuite, he cry a bit at the notary
- I understand people worry, Mile End lost many small shops, but a scam?? 17 years on the street, that hurt
- the cousin of Marc-Antoine is half right, the building was sold — to me!
- invite everybody to the reopening Saturday January 23, coffee and a piece of the new bread free
- thank Priya and the ones who defend us
- if somebody really want the money back for the carnet they can come and I give it back, no question

Thread: Pétrin Doré on Fairmount closing?? sign in the window
(I'm Pétrin Doré (Hélène) here. I'm replying to D. Bergeron's message of 2026-12-28T11:47:00.)

---

From: jules_on_waverly | 2026-12-28T08:41:00
Walked by Pétrin Doré this morning and there's a sign taped on the door: "Fermé du 4 au 18 janvier. Grande nouvelle bientôt!" plus the shelves looked half empty. Anyone know what's going on? Please don't tell me we're losing the only place that still does a proper pain de campagne around here.

---

From: Marc-Antoine L. | 2026-12-28T09:15:00
My cousin works in real estate, he says the whole building at that corner was sold in the fall. Ground floor commercial + 3 apartments. You know what that usually means... condos and a bank or a vape shop downstairs. "Grande nouvelle" lol. Sad if true.

---

From: noodle_and_crumb | 2026-12-28T10:02:00
Not to be that person but didn't they sell those prepaid bread books in October? Like 12 loaves up front? Collect a bunch of cash right before the holidays then put up a "closed" sign. I'm not saying it's on purpose but the timing is not great. I bought one and I have 7 loaves left on it.

---

From: Priya S. | 2026-12-28T10:30:00
Come on, the woman has been there since like 2009, she knows half the street by name. She gave my kid a free chocolatine every Saturday for a year. I really doubt it's a scam. Could just be vacation? Bakers work 6 days a week, they're allowed two weeks off.

---

[the message I'm replying to] From: D. Bergeron | 2026-12-28T11:47:00
I'm a regular too and I like her, but honestly people paid $60 for those carnets and now there's a vague sign and rumours about the building. A two-week vacation doesn't need a "big news soon". Mme Gagnon, I know you read this board sometimes. If you're closing or moving, people deserve a straight answer before the 4th, not a surprise. What happens to the carnets?

(About me: bakery owner, 57, Montreal, Canada. Length: it should come to roughly 800-2,000 words.)

must_cover: Explains that the bakery bought the building and is temporarily closing for renovations.
States the January 19 reopening at 7 a.m. and invites everyone to the January 23 celebration with free coffee and a piece of the new bread.
Explains that carnets remain valid without expiry, each holder gets one free croissant in January, and anyone wanting a refund can get one on request, no questions asked.
Thanks Priya and the other supporters and reassures upstairs tenants that their tenancies and rent remain unchanged.
